prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Kansas City Missouri for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t browse current reviews to name a single definitive “best” lawyer, and “best” depends on your case facts and priorities (trial experience, max recoveries, communication style, etc.). I can, however, show you how to find the strongest personal injury attorney in Kansas City, MO and what to ask so you can pick the best one for your car-accident case.

How to find top Kansas City car-accident lawyers
- Use reputable directories and ratings: Super Lawyers, Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Lawyers.com, and Google Business reviews.  
- Contact the Missouri Bar’s lawyer referral service or the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association for referrals.  
- Look for attorneys or firms that specialize in car-accident/personal-injury claims (not general practice).  
- Check reported verdicts and settlements (often listed on firm websites or news articles).  

What to look for
- Substantial experience in car-accident cases and a high percentage of practice devoted to personal injury.  
- Trial experience (many cases settle, but trial readiness strengthens your position).  
- Clear contingency-fee agreement and transparent explanation of fees/costs.  
- Good client communication (responsiveness, clear timelines).  
- Positive client reviews and peer recognition (Super Lawyers, AVVO rating, Martindale AV Preeminent).  

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident cases? How many similar cases have you handled?  
- What percentage of your practice is personal injury? Do you take cases on contingency? What is your contingency fee and what costs are deducted?  
- Who will handle my case (attorney or paralegal)? Will you go to trial if needed?  
- What is your track record for recoveries in cases like mine? Can you provide references or past verdicts/settlements?  
- What information/documents do you need from me right now? What is the likely timeline?  
- How will you communicate updates and how often?  

What to bring to a consultation
- Police report, medical records and bills, photos of damage/injuries, contact info for witnesses, insurance info (yours and other driver’s), correspondence with insurers, pay stubs if lost wages, and any demand letters/offers.

Fee expectations and practical points
- Most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency fees range (commonly around one‑third to 40% depending on whether suit is filed or tried). Ask how costs (expert fees, court costs) are handled.  
- Preserve evidence, get medical care, document everything, and act promptly — there are time limits and evidence preservation issues.

Red flags
- Promises of a specific dollar amount or guaranteed results.  
- No written fee agreement.  
- Poor responsiveness or lack of clarity about who’ll handle the day-to-day work.  
- Very low review counts or lots of unresolved complaints with the state bar.

If you want, I can:
- Give a short list of well-reviewed Kansas City personal-injury firms if you want search tips I can teach you to run. (I can’t pull current web results, but I can show precise search queries and sources to check.)  
- Draft an email or script you can use to contact multiple lawyers or a checklist of documents to bring to consultations.

Would you like help finding a shortlist for your ZIP code, or would you like a draft message to send to potential attorneys?
